messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping—you can feel it in the air, the way people are talking now like they’ve forgotten to be afraid. But the security forces aren’t backing down; they’re just waiting, and the money’s still flowing where it needs to. The question isn’t if something’s coming—it’s whether we’re ready when it does."*"
Sender 2: "*"Listen—this isn’t just another wave of frustration. The cracks are everywhere: the elites are suddenly singing from the same hymn sheet, the security forces are watching *each other*, and even the taxi drivers are talking like this is a matter of *when*, not *if*. The regime’s choking on its own lies, and the hospitals running out of supplies is the last straw—people aren’t just angry, they’re *ready*. But we need to move carefully. The military’s silence? That’s the wild card. If we’re going to act, it has to be soon—and it has to be smart."*"
Sender 3: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s leaning harder—like a tree in a storm that hasn’t fallen yet. The real question isn’t if it’ll crack, but whether the wind picks up before the roots give out."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—elites aren’t even pretending to play nice anymore, the security forces are waiting for orders that might never come, and even the shopkeeper down the street is talking like this is inevitable. The regime’s still paying pensions and running exports, but that’s just the last gasp of a machine that’s running on fumes. We’re not at the end yet, but we’re past the point of no return."*"
Sender 5: "*"Listen—this isn’t just cracks in the walls anymore. The regime’s holding its breath, not its ground. The elites are circling the wagons, the streets are quiet but *alive*, and the money’s already halfway out the door. Either they’re about to make a move—or they’re already losing the game and just don’t want us to notice yet. Either way, we’re in the eye of the storm. Stay sharp, stay ready."*"
Sender 6: "*"The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing—payments are late, the security forces are slipping, and even the elites are whispering instead of barking orders. The question isn’t *if* things will break, but *how*—whether it’s a slow unraveling or a sudden snap. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The right moment hasn’t come… but it’s coming."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, it’s all still in play—no one’s fully committed yet. The elites are hedging, the streets are quiet but not settled, and the security forces are waiting for a signal. Either the regime’s playing it cool to avoid panic, or they’re one wrong move away from chaos. Stay sharp—this could break fast."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—things are unraveling faster than we thought. The elite are panicking, the security forces are cracking, and the streets are quieter than they should be. If we’re going to move, it has to be soon."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now. The regime’s scrambling to keep up appearances, but the cracks are in the foundation, not just the paint. Stay sharp, stay ready, and watch for the moment when the facade finally gives way."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the signs are all over the place—some say the walls are crumbling, others say they’re just tightening the screws. The patrols are pulling back from the usual hotspots, but the money’s still flowing into construction, like they’re either bracing for something or trying to look like they’re in control. The young ones are itching for a spark, but the old guard’s whispering to hold steady. Either way, the regime’s sweating—you can feel it in the air, even if they’re still screaming ‘everything’s fine.’ Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We need to see which way the wind breaks first."*"
Sender 11: "*"Listen—this isn’t just another rough patch. The palace is eerily quiet, the soldiers are chatting with civilians instead of barking orders, and even the shopkeepers are dropping hints like they’ve got nothing left to lose. Something’s coming, and soon. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are openly fighting, the army’s barely holding itself together, and even the ministry staff are packing bags. The regime’s not just weak; it’s *panicking*. The only question now is whether it collapses fast or drags us all down with it first."*"
Sender 13: "*"The regime’s grip is loosening—patrols are pulling back from trouble spots, jokes are getting bolder, and even the censors are scrambling to keep up. But don’t mistake hesitation for collapse; they’re still in the game, just playing a weaker hand. The real question isn’t *if* they’ll crack down again, but whether they’ll have the strength to make it stick."*"
Sender 14: "*"Listen—something’s shifting, but I don’t know if it’s the start of the unraveling or just the regime tightening its grip before the next squeeze. The fear’s still there, but people are talking anyway, and that’s the dangerous part. Stay sharp this month—three separate people have warned me the same thing, and the embassies are already moving like they know more than we do."*"
Sender 15: "*"The facade is holding, but the foundation’s shifting—elites are too busy circling each other to patch things up, the troops are restless, and the money’s not moving like it used to. The regime’s still putting on a show, but the script’s getting harder to follow, and the audience is starting to notice."*"
Sender 16: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure when it’ll come down, but everyone can feel the floor shifting under their feet. The fear’s still there, but now the real risk is staying quiet while the rest of us start talking."*"
Sender 17: "*"The cracks are showing—small things, but they’re there. The leadership is scrambling behind closed doors, the streets are getting louder, and even the border guards aren’t following orders like they used to. It’s not over yet, but something’s shifting—just don’t ask me which way."*"
Sender 18: "*"Something’s off—top brass are holding it together for now, but the cracks are showing. The streets are quiet, but the silence feels like a held breath, not surrender. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We need to watch how the security forces react next."*"
Sender 19: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet of a machine running too smoothly, like someone’s oiled the gears but forgot to check the fuel. The elites are locking ranks, the borders are being prepped for something, and even the pharmacist is stocking up—*not* *selling. But the streets? The doctors, the teachers? They’re waking up. The question isn’t if, but when the script starts to crack. And when it does, we need to be ready—not to push, but to *move*."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are digging in, not running, and even the security forces are shifting their weight. The regime’s grip is slipping, but no one knows how fast or what comes next—just that staying quiet might be the riskier move now."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are definitely thinner now—people are talking louder, the jokes are sharper, and even the security forces seem to be saving their energy for something. But here’s the thing: no one’s running *yet*, and the top is still holding together—just slower, like a machine running on fumes. Could be the calm before the collapse, or just the regime tightening its belt to ride this out. Either way, we’re in the stretch where one wrong move could tip it either way. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—this isn’t just another crackdown or a blip. The cracks are spreading, but the real shift is that people *know* it now, and they’re moving differently. The regime’s still got teeth, but the ship’s drifting, and the crew’s starting to notice. Stay sharp—this could go fast."*"
Sender 23: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping, but they’re not done yet—everyone’s still playing it safe, but the cracks are showing. If we’re going to move, it has to be soon, before they figure out how to tighten things back up."*"
Sender 24: "*"It feels like we’re all holding our breath—no one’s running for the exits, but no one’s fully committed to staying either. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are in the *hesitation*—elites hedging, security forces saving their strength, even the banks moving money like they’re not sure which way the wind will blow. Something’s coming, but I don’t think anyone’s decided yet if it’s a storm or just another false alarm."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the machine’s still humming—no glitches in the system, no panic in the ranks, and the elites are doubling down on their bets here, not bolting. But that doesn’t mean it’s *stable*—just that no one’s willing to be the first to pull the thread. The real question is whether the quiet’s because the fight’s over… or because it’s just waiting for the right moment to start again."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
